name: Stampe SV.4
summary: Belgian 1930s two-seat trainer and aerobatic biplane, built after the war by Nord in France; a popular antique aerobat in Europe and a rarity in the US.

wings: Staggered single-bay biplane with ailerons on all four wing panels
Upper wing swept back over a straighter lower wing
engines: Inverted inline four-cylinder de Havilland Gipsy Major with a neat narrow nose

tellTales: Biplane with ailerons on both upper and lower wings
Narrow inline-engine nose with two tandem open cockpits
Compact aerobatic trainer with a swept upper wing and four ailerons

confusedWith.howToTell: The Tiger Moth has swept-back wings with lower-wing ailerons only; the Stampe has ailerons on all four wing panels.
Both have four ailerons; the Jungmann has swept-back upper and lower wings of near-equal span while the Stampe has a swept upper wing over a straighter lower wing.
The Stearman is much larger with a bare radial; the Stampe is a small inline-engine biplane.
